issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The same source tree produces different RL artifact fingerprints on macOS,
Linux CI, and a Linux container — so the identity-pin tests
(`test_evaluation_identity`,
`test_presets_match_revisioned_native_configs` in
`experiments/post_training/rl_tests/test_rl.py`) can only be authored against
one environment. CI re-pins then break local runs and vice versa; this forced
re-pin churn in #11898 and again in #11659.

Root cause (narrowed): the fingerprint path emits

```
WARNING fingerprint: no canonical form for evalrecords.records.EvaluationSelection;
using a best-effort stable fallback. Register one via
marin.execution.fingerprint.register_fingerprint for an exact fingerprint.
```

(and the same for `EvaluationOverrides`) while computing these corpora. The
"best-effort stable fallback" is not stable across environments, so the pin is
hashing environment-dependent bytes.

Reproduce (tree: `benfeuer/rl-curriculum-artifact` @ 82dc79bbb4, whose CI merge
ref is that commit with main @ a8a38d6e6d):

1. macOS 15 arm64, env from `uv sync --all-packages --extra cpu --extra dedup
   --group test`:

   ```
   .venv/bin/pytest experiments/post_training/test_evaluation_identity.py \
     -q -o addopts="--import-mode=importlib"
   ```

   Passes; the fingerprints are the pins recorded in the test (`a0268301`,
   `3b56f26e`, `34198f43`).

2. Linux x86_64, python:3.12 container, env from the same sync command:

   ```
   docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v <tree>:/repo -w /repo python:3.12 \
     bash -c "pip install uv && uv sync --all-packages --extra cpu --extra dedup \
     --group test --frozen && .venv/bin/pytest \
     experiments/post_training/test_evaluation_identity.py \
     -o addopts='--import-mode=importlib -vv'"
   ```

   Fails with `65f9cd98`, `5f315156`, `dd263248` — three different values from
   the same tree. CI-Linux on the same merge ref agrees with the container
   ([job 136704096210](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44857643177/job/136704096210)).

3. Cross-check that the pins are stable on Linux for clean main: the same
   container invocation at 18ed6c31a7 passes with the recorded pins, so the
   fallback happens to agree there; the instability shows on the tree above.

Expected: identical trees produce identical artifact fingerprints on every
platform and environment. Register canonical fingerprint forms for
`evalrecords.records.EvaluationSelection` and `EvaluationOverrides` (per the
warning's own instruction, via
`marin.execution.fingerprint.register_fingerprint`), or make the fallback
content-based and environment-independent; then re-pin once.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

[`eval_step()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2bf3f721c9/experiments/evaluation/pipeline.py#L148-L156) hashes the evaluation selections and producer artifact identities; each [producer identity](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2bf3f721c9/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/lazy.py#L286-L288) includes another fingerprint. The [fallback encoder](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2bf3f721c9/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/fingerprint.py#L140-L158) warns and serializes `vars()` for these models. That warning does not identify which JSON field differs. The report says clean main passes on Linux, while [#11659](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11659) adds `curriculum_identity` to an upstream SkyRL config, so the producer payload needs comparison too.

**Proposed fix**

1. At `82dc79bbb4`, capture `fingerprint_payload()` for all three evaluation steps and their producer steps on macOS and Linux with the same `uv.lock`. Diff the parsed JSON and record the first divergent field.
2. Canonicalize that field at its source. If it is an evalrecords model field, register explicit encoders for `EvaluationSelection` and `EvaluationOverrides`; if it is in a producer config, fix that config. Add a regression for the differing value.
3. Run both identity-pin tests on macOS and Linux, re-pin once from matching payloads, and coordinate the pin edit with #11659 before publishing a `Fixes #11932` PR.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 I reproduced this on Linux, and the macOS values are what this tree computes when `marin` is imported from main.

- On Linux (x86_64, Python 3.12, the same `uv sync`), `82dc79bbb4` gives `65f9cd98`, `5f315156`, `dd263248`, as in your container and CI. Main at `a8a38d6e6d`, which the branch merged, gives `a0268301`, `3b56f26e`, `34198f43`. Those three pins came into the branch with the merge of main (`bf8b110e2`) and stayed in the test until `6c69e08a9` and `091973b1d`.
- I walked the three evaluation steps' dependencies and diffed every `fingerprint_payload()` between the two trees. The only root change is the `curriculum_identity: null` key that `c50b551e4` adds to the four SkyRL training configs (`iceball-micro-rl`, `skyrl-port-smoke/train` and `/resume`, `curriculum-rl/naive-smoke`). Every other difference is a dependency fingerprint embedded downstream, and the `EvaluationSelection` and `EvaluationOverrides` entries are identical. So with this branch's code all three evaluation fingerprints change on every platform.
- On the head `091973b1d`, `test_evaluation_identity.py` and both `test_presets_match_revisioned_native_configs` cases pass. With `PYTHONPATH` set to main's `lib/marin/src`, all three fail, and the evaluation test gets exactly `a0268301`, `3b56f26e`, `34198f43`.
- The fallback serializes the two models' `vars()`, which are plain values here, and `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0 to 5 gave the same fingerprints. Registering canonical encoders would remove the warning but not change these values.

So the macOS run likely imported `marin` from another checkout. From the tree, `.venv/bin/python -c "import marin; print(marin.__file__)"` should print that tree's `lib/marin/src/marin/__init__.py`. The pins at `091973b1d` are this branch's own values.

issues.title: RL artifact fingerprints are environment-dependent (macOS vs Linux vs container)

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A 6-hour optimization sprint (started 2026-11-21 ~13:45 UTC / 8:45 AM EST) measured Mochi (535B-A23B) decode and rollout throughput on GB200s and **selected the training geometry: EP16/DP16/TP1, seq64, HBM 0.85, batch 8192 (A10, 48 trainer + 16 rollout = 64 GB200)** — 2.169x the `.103` control's per-GPU rollout rate. Best pure-decode serving result: EP16/seqs64/HBM90 at 831.73 tok/s/GPU (a fixed-prompt-pool upper bound, not a training gain). The real Mochi RL training launch is planned for 2026-11-21 ~19:45 UTC (14:45 EST) on cw-us-east-08a. This issue is maintained by the secretary agent from the worker's REPORT.md/STATUS.md; every measured arm is recorded below with reproduction details.

## Description

Context: the long-loop plan needs ~50B SFT tokens in a 20 h stage plus RL rounds on Mochi. Today Mochi decodes ~10 tok/s per request and ~25 tok/s per GB200 at eval concurrency, and Mochi SFT trains ~143–177k tok/s per rack (#8089: 29.3 s/step on 11 racks). The sprint replaces back-of-envelope ceilings (decode ~2–4k tok/s/GPU BF16 at large batch; training ~2–3x the current rate) with measurements.

Two lanes:

- **A — real-RL rollout arms**: full round-runner RL jobs (48 trainer + 12 rollout GB200, two optimizer updates), measuring rollout throughput under admission knobs; each arm is cancelled after its measured 25-min window.
- **B — pure-decode capacity arms**: no trainer; the checked-in long-loop throughput worker serves a 6.4k-prompt / 1k-output synthetic workload (plus replay variants) and measures sustained decode; arms run to a valid counter window then are cancelled.

Fixed infrastructure for all arms: cluster `cw-us-east-08a`, PRODUCTION priority, GB200 GPUs, rack r136 hard-excluded, one-NVLink-gang placement, BF16, FLASH_ATTN + triton MoE, prefix caching, compilation + PIECEWISE CUDA graphs on.

Workload-shape caveat for the B serving lane: the fixed-pool shared8 arms use 32 prompt bodies / 256 request identities at 6,439 input / 1,024 output tokens (long) or 139 input (short); repeated cycles can overstate fresh-RL prefix reuse. Pure serving runs use 12 GPUs unless the arm name says EP16 (then 16). All B arms use 0 Daytona vCPU.

### Reproduction

- Repo: `marin-community/marin`, branch `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` and sprint branch `benfeuer/mochi-throughput`.
- Round configs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-throughput-*.yaml` (default-2update, inflight128, staleness11, engine32-kv85, harbor1024, harbor384, ep16-seqs64, ep16-seqs64-kv90, ep16-httpid-control, noquotas, kv-fp8, **ep16-demand512** `.118`, **train** `.115`; the retired workers128 config was deleted unlaunched).
- Decode specs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/mochi-decode-*.json` (seqs16 control through the ep16 variants).
- Launch commands:
  - Real-RL arm: `uv run --no-sync python -m experiments.post_training.long_loop.round_runner --round experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/<arm>.yaml --source-revision <git-sha> --validation-output <path> --through rl --run`
  - Pure-decode arm: `uv run --no-sync python -m experiments.post_training.long_loop.throughput` with the pinned spec JSON, submitted via the standard Iris CLI (source-pinned launch specs under `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-throughput/launches/<sha>/`).
- Source revisions: v103 `b0a9727622d54a75101c455f3e304d6ae3003565`; seqs32 `.104` `46063946b49d9d677f5aa0c94a26f27715550764`; A1 `.105` `476a95362f35014e5d092ebd79adfcd542cb5105`; A2 `.106` `3bc5ae3fda43203232aa2c2dc019e8abeea5a69d`; A3 `.107` and first EP16 pair `3a859712f51d3ddff46748e850208e8315dc53da`; harbor1024 `.108` config-landed `e0bf304558d4fdbf3b41a9b68285918eb19ca1ca` (actually submitted at `3f4a4c68ce…`); harbor384 `.109` `c6515fbdc7bc2b51f0f43649dac08ee54fa3397d`; workers128 `.110` `7f245b01735ced953e3ce490db8bca9159bc0d1f`; `.110`-default3 re-land `8aee017ea5cfcd9748c372fc8555be2c8483f757`; B kv90 landing `530ab73b76a28a3e15a741d8f946a0dfaeea8818`; `.111` real EP16 arm `058da8dcc2332525d6245ba8f7bae6ea18308b4c`; `.112` quota-free `aab5e5f57bfa1ef5a6cb3c599ba40302a8e92247`; `.113` A9 kv90 real with header fix `858ab5d15bf3118ae0358ff79569ec6b33320a68`; `.113`-recipe landing `f26fc27bcd86dac16bcf867435f72ef9166cf463`; final-gates landing `cf7e04df26c99f74e52d5c39e3cb7b6e593ea8e1`; **selected-training landing `5957d8bbcf0cd945243cdd544eb4433f7e36ac88`**; A11 FP8-KV `ce13e39e8435a9149a1268d6b25db54c32f75411`; A13 demand-512 `dd0250dc1a65a3e04c2f6b0d2f79ea55511a506f`; **relaunch `.119` `ccf0bdc3561be7b3a6d407b3c95af03fbf37f2c4`**; **correction `.120` `6a118946e605a3eba586b0d256139a6690a859cc`**; quota-free fix `30d6357c550d35617b49e9f0c630c3754d7c87f2`; observation fix `3226044a8fcf1dacad4b022074f94784493f83b7`; Daytona ownership metric `8b1e1686a985691f9454ed2c01c757c79f3ec736`; context-gap fix `119ea9984b7e400e926ced96bc8a4a3f8df0a11b`; latest B pair `3f4a4c68ce4fad43d1a639d1d390d1ae3e3649b1`; pure-decode implementation landing `e9a16e37ce65754192208551df44e972e8c9de7b`. Per-arm B serving sources differ (KV85 `f91a4966b6…`, batch16384 `476a95362f…`, shared8 pair `d08bf17b3a…`, seqs64 pair `3bc5ae3fda…`) — the machine-readable index is `secretary-arm-provenance-20261121.json` in the evidence folder.
- Counters: the engine-side Finelog sink registered by SkyRL's `inference_stats` callback (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/callbacks/builtin.py:1253` and `:1108`; `inference_observability.py:130`), read as reset-safe cumulative deltas over fixed windows. A1–A3 lack native `generation_tokens_total` because the recipes' explicit callback list makes `create_default_callbacks` return early, so their rates are console-sample estimates (marked * in the table). The callback is added from A4 and the training config onward. Example queries: `decode-control-live-samples-1308.jsonl` + `analyze_decode_live.py` (control window 12:58:49–13:07:52 UTC: 1,341,242 generated-token increments over 542.47 s = 2,472.48 tok/s aggregate), `a3-first25-analysis.json`.
- Receipts: `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/mochi-throughput/...` (Filer links below) and local evidence folder `/Users/benfeuer/Documents/experiments/active/mochi-throughput/`.

### Rollout concurrency (code trace)

- `TaskRolloutWorker` holds `task_slots` and `harbor_task_slots` semaphores (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py:390-391`), acquired per task (`:548-552`); the Harbor semaphore wraps the entire `engine.run_task`.
- Harbor `n_concurrent_trials` is consumed at `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inline_harbor_client.py:119`.
- Documented rule: slots = Harbor `n_concurrent_trials` (16 when unset) // num workers (`lib/skyrlrecipe/src/skyrlrecipe/sections.py:458`); config key `terminal_bench.harbor.n_concurrent_trials` (`experiments/post_training/long_loop/stage_config.py:38`). For the 256-slot config that is 8/worker; Harbor384 gives 12/worker.
- Precision: the 8-slot semaphore is one group's worth, not an atomic group lock — partial groups can interleave; dispatch `min(_pending)` has no Harbor-slot awareness, and the generic 1024/worker task slots are unbinding.
- Measurement limit: no explicit Harbor-semaphore wait logs are emitted, and A5's bounded logs contain 0 direct slot-wait records, so actual Harbor occupancy is NOT measured; A3's 128 group calls / 430 pending model requests do not count Harbor occupancy.
- Staleness admission: `FullBatch.lease_batch` uses `range(step, step + staleness + 1)`, so staleness can change admission during step 1 even without a policy update (this corrects an earlier blanket "never binds" statement; the A2 causal-gain claim remains withdrawn and default staleness 3 is kept per direction).
- Consumed route quotas require `batch_policy: full_batch` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/buffer.py:49,72`; `lib/skyrlrecipe/src/skyrlrecipe/sections.py:440,444`).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Pick the real Mochi RL training config from measurements: rollout throughput as a function of admission knobs (inflight workers, max_staleness_steps, Harbor slots) and decode throughput as a function of engine knobs (max_num_seqs, HBM/KV utilization, expert parallelism, shared-prefix layout, batched tokens). Decision rule (user ruling): config changes only — no engine code changes.

## Status

- Sprint clock: started ~13:45 UTC 2026-11-21; training selection 19:30 UTC (14:30 EST); real RL launch 19:45 UTC (14:45 EST).
- Current **provisional training candidate** (worker statement, 13:43 EST / 18:45 UTC): **EP12, seq32, HBM 0.85, batch 8192, Harbor 256, workers 32, inflight128, staleness 3, graphs/prefix caching ON** — the quota on/off choice pends the 19:30 evidence (A9/A10 finals). Framing: A3's engine first-25min estimate (127.22/GPU vs the `.103` control's 55.90) is a 2.28x OBSERVED short-window/proxy (staleness 11 in A3 is not retained for training); A8's quota-off 208.63/GPU is a 3.73x OBSERVED raw rate but with 0 consumed batches / 90 nonagentic completions, so it is NOT a training gain. Earlier "current training candidate" notes are superseded by this reconciled statement.
- Two follow-up decode arms in flight at source `3f4a4c68ce`: EP16/seqs128/shared8 (`/benfeuer/mochi-throughput-decode-ep16-seqs128-shared8-20261121a`) and EP16/seqs64/batch4096/shared8 (`/benfeuer/mochi-throughput-decode-ep16-seqs64-batch4096-shared8-20261121a`).
- In flight at ~17:10 UTC: A5/Harbor384 engine init completed 17:09 UTC (no generation counter window yet; startup receipts `sprint-current-startup-1709.jsonl`, `sprint-a5-live-1709.jsonl`); both B EP16 arms loaded weights 17:07–17:09 UTC (`sprint-b-live-1709.jsonl`). A B HBM 0.90 arm was then submitted in parallel (`/benfeuer/mochi-throughput-decode-ep16-seqs64-kv90-shared8-20261121a`, 16 GB200, source `530ab73b76a28a3e15a741d8f946a0dfaeea8818`, spec `mochi-decode-ep16-seqs64-kv90-shared8.json` — only change HBM 0.85→0.90 versus the completed EP16/seqs64 552.15 tok/s/GPU baseline), since A60 + B16×3 = 108 ≤ the 128-GPU cap.
- **B batch4096 FINAL** (valid 1500.818 s window, zero failed requests; 18,553 overlapping requests valid; drain 123.564 s): 12,016.76 aggregate / **751.05 tok/s/GPU**, request arithmetic mean 12.21 tok/s, 61.59/64 running, KV 52.41% mean / 65.58% max, TTFT 3.20 s, prefix hit 99.76% — **+36.02%** over the EP16/seqs64 batch8192 baseline (552.15/GPU; request 9.27→12.21, KV 85.43→52.41, prefix 48.86→99.76). This fixed-32-shared-prompt-pool cache-fit gain is NOT yet a real-RL gain (receipt `pure-ep16-batch4096-result.json`; final artifact `decode/ep16-seqs64-kv85-batch4096-shared8-20261121a/synthetic-context64-output1024-shared8-seed17-c1024.json`). **Correction (~20:15 UTC): kv90's final 831.73/GPU is the best valid long-B** — batch4096's 751.05 is second; the early kv90 provisional (844.22) had overstated its final. Sequencing: A7 runs its specified batch 8192 first; the best one-knob B candidate follows in real rollouts.

## TL;DR

A 6-hour optimization sprint (started 2026-11-21 ~13:45 UTC / 8:45 AM EST) is measuring Mochi (535B-A23B) decode and rollout throughput on GB200s to pick the config for the first real long-loop RL training run. Best real-rollout arm so far: A3 `engine32-kv85` (inflight128, staleness11, seqs32, HBM 0.85) at 127.22 tok/s/GPU over its first 25 min — 2.28x the v103 control (55.90). Best pure-decode arm: EP16/seqs64/shared8 at 552.15 tok/s/GPU (16 GPUs). The real Mochi RL training launch is planned for 2026-11-21 ~19:45 UTC (14:45 EST) on cw-us-east-08a. This issue is maintained by the secretary agent from the worker's REPORT.md/STATUS.md; every measured arm is recorded below with reproduction details.

## Description

Context: the long-loop plan needs ~50B SFT tokens in a 20 h stage plus RL rounds on Mochi. Today Mochi decodes ~10 tok/s per request and ~25 tok/s per GB200 at eval concurrency, and Mochi SFT trains ~143–177k tok/s per rack (#8089: 29.3 s/step on 11 racks). The sprint replaces back-of-envelope ceilings (decode ~2–4k tok/s/GPU BF16 at large batch; training ~2–3x the current rate) with measurements.

Two lanes:

- **A — real-RL rollout arms**: full round-runner RL jobs (48 trainer + 12 rollout GB200, two optimizer updates), measuring rollout throughput under admission knobs; each arm is cancelled after its measured 25-min window.
- **B — pure-decode capacity arms**: no trainer; the checked-in long-loop throughput worker serves a 6.4k-prompt / 1k-output synthetic workload (plus replay variants) and measures sustained decode; arms run to a valid counter window then are cancelled.

Fixed infrastructure for all arms: cluster `cw-us-east-08a`, PRODUCTION priority, GB200 GPUs, rack r136 hard-excluded, one-NVLink-gang placement, BF16, FLASH_ATTN + triton MoE, prefix caching, compilation + PIECEWISE CUDA graphs on.

### Reproduction

- Repo: `marin-community/marin`, branch `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` and sprint branch `benfeuer/mochi-throughput`.
- Round configs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-throughput-*.yaml` (default-2update, inflight128, staleness11, engine32-kv85, harbor1024, harbor384).
- Decode specs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/mochi-decode-*.json` (seqs16 control through the ep16 variants).

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
`MarinSkyRL:nemotron_if` maps each Nemotron IFEval instruction to an open-instruct checker in `skyrl/scorers/ifeval_utils.py` (`NEMOTRON_CONSTRAINTS` in `skyrl/ifeval.py`). For three instructions the checker's rule differs from the prompt's wording, so a reply that does what the prompt says fails the constraint. The source is 15% of the RL groups in the Exp4 curriculum (#11681), whose pools Exp5 reuses.

| Instruction | Prompt | Checker | Rows that fail |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `length_constraints:number_paragraphs` | "Paragraphs are separated with the markdown divider: ***" | `verify_paragraph_count` splits on `* * *` only, so a reply divided by `***` has one paragraph | 4,515 (every row that asks for 2 or more) |
| the same rows that also ask for an exact `number_bullet_lists` | "exactly N bullet points ... such as: * This is point 1." | `verify_bullet_points` counts every line that starts with `*`, so each `***` divider line is a bullet too | 1,211 of 1,218 lose both constraints |
| `multiple_sections` with `detectable_format:title` | "Mark the beginning of each section with SECTION X" | `validate_sections` counts the text before the first marker as a section, so a `<<title>>` line above `SECTION 1` adds one | 554 |

Two more differences depend on how a reply is formatted. A line that opens with markdown bold, such as `**Key points:**`, counts as a bullet, and 15,316 rows ask for an exact bullet count. `validate_highlighted_sections` counts each `**bold**` span twice, so half the requested highlights pass; 19,355 rows ask for two or more.

The counts are over the pinned file (`nvidia/Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset` at `ab2a40d2`, `RL/instruction_following/instruction_following.jsonl`, 56,339 rows) run through `nemotron_constraint` and `normalize_ground_truth` at `cd0e932c7`, which keep 54,954 rows; the Exp4 pool in `exp4_data.py` records 54,953. For each kept row I built replies from the row's own arguments and the prompt's wording and scored them against the row's constraints. 4,625 of the 4,723 prompts with the paragraph instruction write the divider as `***`, and none writes only `* * *`. verifyit's IFEval checks (`lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py`) pass every one of these replies.

On the 4,515 paragraph rows, a reply that follows the instruction and a reply that ignores it both fail the constraint, so it gives RL no signal toward following it; only a reply that happens to use `* * *` passes.

Reproduce from the repository root with plain `python`:

```python
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/scorers")
import ifeval_utils as checks

reply = "First paragraph.\n\n***\n\nSecond paragraph."
print(checks.verify_paragraph_count(reply, 2))  # False
print(checks.verify_paragraph_count(reply.replace("***", "* * *"), 2))  # True

with_bullets = "First paragraph.\n* One\n* Two\n\n***\n\nSecond paragraph."
print(checks.verify_bullet_points(with_bullets, 2))  # False: the divider line also starts with *

titled = "<<A Title>>\n\nSECTION 1\nBody.\n\nSECTION 2\nBody."
print(checks.validate_sections(titled, 2, "SECTION"))  # False: the title line counts as a section
```

Expected: a reply that follows the prompt's wording passes these constraints.

cc @penfever @chrismc91

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The two open-instruct copies still score RLVR-IFeval task curation and SkyRL's IFEval data contract; #11983 changed only the task-curation copy, while #11979 moved `nemotron_if` to verifyit. The evaluation `IFEVAL_GRADER` packages a separate lm-evaluation-harness checker through TaskCompendium, so the requested “every grader” scope also includes its strict and loose metrics. No open PR found for #11984 or this migration.

**Relevant code**
- [`skyrl/ifeval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9c51ba379/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/ifeval.py#L138) — RLVR conversion and source versions.
- [`skyrl/ifeval_grade.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9c51ba379/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/ifeval_grade.py#L19) — task-curation scoring entry point.
- [`data_contracts.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9c51ba379/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/data_contracts.py#L64) — SkyRL normalization and preflight.
- [`scorers/instructions.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9c51ba379/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/instructions.py#L75) — evaluation strict/loose reduction.
- [`grade_ifeval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a9c51ba379/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_ifeval.py#L57) — canonical candidate checker.

# Proposed Fix

## Design

Add one verifyit boundary for SkyRL's 25 `func_name` descriptors. Map each name and required argument to a verifyit constraint, reject unknown or incomplete descriptors during dataset preparation, and grade each constraint independently so the existing fraction-of-constraints reward remains intact. Runtime grading should return zero for malformed input or checker failure. This mapping is necessary because the SkyRL descriptors use function names and `N`, while verifyit uses instruction IDs and named parameters.

Move `rlvr_ifeval` conversion and its grader script to that boundary; remove the shipped `ifeval_utils.py` and update the source description and vendoring record. Move SkyRL's `ifeval` contract and environment to the same boundary, then delete `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/ifeval/utils.py`. Keep the existing reward fields and complete-pass preflight contract.

Switch the TaskCompendium HARNESS profile to verifyit checks while retaining its eight strict/loose response variants, per-instruction flags, metric names, and metric weights. Remove the separate harness checker implementation once all its callers are gone; leave IFBench's distinct checkers in place. `IFEVAL_GRADER` is an environment definition, but its packaged scorer and dependency set must change with this path.

## Score and artifact policy

The known score-changing sources are `MarinSkyRL:rlvr_ifeval` and the SkyRL `ifeval` environment because their open-instruct checks will change. Canonical `Evalchemy:ifeval` scores may also change when its harness checks move; compare them before claiming parity. Bump affected curation recipe and evaluation protocol versions and record per-source score deltas in the PR. If any frozen Micro210 policy score changes, create a new policy version; do not edit the frozen score in place.

## Verification

Exercise the #11978 divider, bullet, title/section, and bold-span cases through task-curation grading, SkyRL normalization/preflight and environment grading, and evaluation strict/loose grading. Pair each passing reply with a reply missing the required content; all paths must fail closed. Add descriptor coverage for all 25 SkyRL functions, run the affected safe tests and pre-PR lint review, and compare pinned-source scores before opening a draft PR.

## Open question

The canonical IFEval evaluation currently reports harness-defined metrics. The proposed migration preserves their names and aggregation but changes the underlying checker semantics; the PR should report the resulting metric deltas for the pinned 541-task corpus.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
`verifyit` math grading raises `ValueError` instead of scoring 0 when the reference and the candidate are chained relations with a different number of terms. verifyit calls math-verify with `raise_on_error=True` (`lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py:73`, `:291`), and math-verify's relational comparison zips the two chains with `strict=True` (huggingface/Math-Verify#93). Any caller that grades a wrong answer of this shape crashes. It ended a NuminaMath-CoT R-task build about four minutes in, when the pool screen graded a reference against a mutated copy of itself.

Reproduce:
1. `cd lib/verifyit`
2. `uv run python -c "from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate, MathSpec; print(grade_math_candidate(MathSpec(expected='1<x<3'), '1<x<3<5'))"`
3. Observe `ValueError: zip() argument 2 is longer than argument 1` from `math_verify/grader.py:329`.

Expected: a scored reward of 0, because the candidate does not match the reference.

A related input crashes the same way: math-verify's relation table has no entry for `Unequality`, so grading `x \neq 3` raises `KeyError: <class 'sympy.core.relational.Unequality'>`.

Done when the chained-relation candidate scores 0, and a `\neq` reference, which no candidate can ever match, fails as `InvalidTask` instead of a raw `KeyError`, with regression tests in `lib/verifyit/tests/test_math_answer.py`.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 ## Research

`math-verify` zips the terms of two chained relations with `strict=True`; `_verify` propagates its `ValueError` for unequal lengths. Its relation table also lacks SymPy `Unequality`: a changed `\neq` candidate raises `KeyError`, while an identical candidate can score 1 even though the reference is unsupported.

**Relevant code**
- [`grade_math.py#L65-L74`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L65-L74) — comparison propagates backend errors
- [`grade_math.py#L295-L310`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L295-L310) — default reference and candidate path
- [`test_math_answer.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/verifyit/tests/test_math_answer.py) — math grading regressions

## Proposed Fix

Reject parsed `Unequality` references before grading any candidate. Score unequal-length chained relations as mismatches before calling `math-verify`; keep timeout and other backend failures visible. Add regressions for both outcomes.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
When the reference of a `math` task does not parse as LaTeX, `grade_math` compares replies with one number taken from the reference text. A reply that is only that number scores 1.0, and the right answer written in a notation that parses can score 0.0. `math_answer_task` admits these references, and they pass the golden control.

`_parse` ([`grade_math.py` L80-L86](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cd0e932c780e0171c5612658faa0f180a851569e/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L80-L86)) wraps the reference in `$...$` and calls math-verify with `LatexExtractionConfig()` and `ExprExtractionConfig()` ([L65](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cd0e932c780e0171c5612658faa0f180a851569e/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_math.py#L65)). The `$...$` match and the expression extractor's number matches have the same priority (300). When latex2sympy rejects the whole expression, math-verify's default `any_match` mode takes the next match of that priority: the rightmost number at the start of the text or after a space or `=`. The module docstring says the `$...$` anchoring is there so that math-verify "reads a whole expression instead of the first bare number it finds". Text with `\text{...}` groups can lose its tail a second way: the default unit normalization of latex2sympy2_extended 1.11.0 (`unit_superscript_regex`, `math_normalization.py` L233) deletes everything from the first `\text{` or `\mbox{` to the end when the text ends in `}`, so `32 \text{ white}, 16 \text{ black}` parses as `32`. The reference check of `math_answer_task` ([`answers.py` L117-L122](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cd0e932c780e0171c5612658faa0f180a851569e/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/convert/answers.py#L125-L130)) raises only when `_parse` returns no expression at all.

Reproduce, from the repository root:

```bash
uv run --package marin-verifyit --extra math python - <<'EOF'
from verifyit.modes.grade_math import grade_math_candidate
from verifyit.spec import MathSpec, MathType

CASES = (
    (r"67.\overline{3}", MathType.SCALAR, ("67", r"67.\overline{4}", r"\frac{202}{3}")),
    (r"\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}.", MathType.SCALAR, ("-1",)),
    (r"2007 + \frac\pi 2", MathType.SCALAR, ("2", r"2007 + \frac{\pi}{2}")),
    (r"\{x \mid 2 < x < 3\}", MathType.SET, ("3", r"\{x \mid 0 < x < 3\}", "(2, 3)")),
    (r"32 \text{ white}, 16 \text{ black}", MathType.SCALAR, ("32", r"32 \text{ white}, 99 \text{ black}")),
)
for reference, math_type, replies in CASES:
    spec = MathSpec(expected=reference, math_type=math_type)
    grade_math_candidate(spec, "")  # the reference check of math_answer_task passes
    print(reference, "|", ", ".join(f"{reply}: {grade_math_candidate(spec, reply).reward}" for reply in replies))
EOF
```

On main `cd0e932c` it prints:

```
67.\overline{3} | 67: 1.0, 67.\overline{4}: 1.0, \frac{202}{3}: 0.0
\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}. | -1: 1.0
2007 + \frac\pi 2 | 2: 1.0, 2007 + \frac{\pi}{2}: 0.0
\{x \mid 2 < x < 3\} | 3: 1.0, \{x \mid 0 < x < 3\}: 1.0, (2, 3): 0.0
32 \text{ white}, 16 \text{ black} | 32: 1.0, 32 \text{ white}, 99 \text{ black}: 1.0
```

All five references are rows of the `MarinSkyRL` math sources (`deepscaler` row 18883, `rlvr_math` rows 6258 and 5433, `deepscaler` row 45, `numina_math` shard 4 row 27517).

I converted every row of four sources, and 30,000 seeded rows of `numina_math`, with each source's own converter on main `ee1844b6`, and counted the references whose value comes from part of their text. I then read the ones that are not plain percentages:

| source | math tasks | value from part of the text | of which `N\%` | the rest, read by hand: value misread / no single answer / value right |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `rlvr_math` | 7,492 | 40 | 31 | 3 / 0 / 6 |
| `hendrycks_math` (algebra) | 1,743 | 9 | 8 | 0 / 0 / 1 |
| `math500` | 500 | 0 | 0 | |
| `deepscaler` | 40,285 | 316 | 234 | 61 / 0 / 21 |
| `numina_math`, 30,000 of 859,494 rows | 27,971 | 1,339 | 482 | 100 of 857 read: 45 / 13 / 42 |

"Value right" means the number read is the answer and only text around it is lost, as in `C) 151` or `0.09 \text{ OR } \frac{9}{100}`. The misread references include repeating decimals (9 in `deepscaler`, `133.\overline{3}` read as 133), mixed-number percentages (`33\frac{1}{3}\%` as 33), clock times (`9:45 a.m.` as 9), matrices followed by a period, set-builder sets, congruences, lists of values or functions (`f(x) = 0 \text{ and } f(x) = x.` as 0), and multiple-choice answers whose option holds an expression (`C) \( ky^2 + 3ky + 2k \)` as 2). The statements, such as `\forall x \in \mathbb{R}, x^2 - ax + 1 \geq 0` (read as 0), have no single answer to compare.

The percentages are read through this path as the number before `\%`: `20` scores 1.0 against `20\%`, and `0.2` scores 0.0. The workspace pins `antlr4-python3-runtime==4.11` ([`pyproject.toml` L127](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cd0e932c780e0171c5612658faa0f180a851569e/pyproject.toml#L131)). latex2sympy2_extended 1.11.0's parser for antlr 4.11 has no `FUNC_GAMMA` rule on `AtomContext`, which `convert_atom` checks before `PERCENT_NUMBER`, so every `\%` fails with `AttributeError: 'AtomContext' object has no attribute 'FUNC_GAMMA'`. With antlr 4.13.2 the same library parses `20\%` as `20/100`; math-verify then accepts `0.2`, and `20` because the number is an integer.

Expected: a reference (or a LIST member) whose whole text does not parse is rejected at conversion as `invalid_reference`, as a reference with no parse is today, or is graded on its whole text. #11510 is about references with no parse; huggingface/Math-Verify#85 reports the same number fallback for a reply with a trailing period. A whole-text check alone would also reject the percentages above while the antlr pin stays at 4.11.

`deepscaler`, `rlvr_math`, `hendrycks_math` and `numina_math` are declared for training and `math500` for evaluation; neither recipe (`snowball-100k.json`, `eval-lite.json`) names them today.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
508 of the 1,000 `time_intervals` rows of the generated Reasoning Gym source grade only on the day they were generated. On a later day [the grade script](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/reasoning_gym_grade.py#L55-L57) exits 1 with `ValueError: Regenerated entry differs from the recorded entry` for every reply, the row's own answer included, and [grading](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L350-L353) records an infrastructure error. [Training](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L191-L209) then leaves the rollout out of the loss. `snowball-100k` draws 20,800 rows of this source; I did not count its `time_intervals` rows.

Reproduce:

1. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   PYTHONHASHSEED=0 uv run --package marin-verifyit --extra reasoning-gym python - <<'EOF'
   import sys

   sys.path.insert(0, "experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym")
   import generate
   import reasoning_gym

   task = "time_intervals"
   data = reasoning_gym.create_dataset(task, size=generate.ROWS_PER_TASK, seed=generate.task_seed(task))
   entry = generate.encoded(data[2])
   print(entry["question"])
   print(entry["metadata"]["start_time"], "|", entry["metadata"]["end_time"])
   time_only = ("time", "time_seconds", "time_ms")
   print(sum(data[index]["metadata"]["task_type"] in time_only for index in range(generate.ROWS_PER_TASK)))
   EOF
   ```

2. The first line is a question with times only: `A meeting started at 01:01:14 and ended at 06:10:42. How long was the meeting? Answer in HH:MM:SS.` The second line is the entry's `metadata.start_time` and `metadata.end_time`. They carry the date of the run, for example `2026-11-16 01:01:14 | 2026-11-16 06:10:42`. The third line is `508`, the number of entries of the task types `time`, `time_seconds` and `time_ms`.
3. The row's contract stores the entry as encoded on the generation day, so on a later day the comparison at L56 fails for these entries.

Expected: a row's own answer scores 1.0 on any day.

`reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 parses the time-only strings with `dateutil.parser.parse` (`reasoning_gym/arithmetic/time_intervals.py` L104-L105), and `dateutil` fills a missing date with the current day in the process's local time. The question and the answer are the same on every day. [The converter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/tasks.py#L261-L262) rejects an entry whose `reproducible` flag is false, but [the generator](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/generate.py#L141-L150) sets that flag by regenerating the entry in the same process, so it is true for these rows.

I did not grade a stored row. I encoded the 1,000 entries with `datetime.now()` fixed to 2026-11-04 inside `dateutil`'s parser and ran the grade script on 2026-11-16: 508 regenerated entries differ from the recorded ones, entry 2 exits 1 on its own answer, and entry 0 (task type `datetime`) prints 1.0. Among the first 200 entries of each of the 104 generated tasks, regenerated on another day and in two other time zones, no other task has entries that pass the `reproducible` flag and differ.

issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
issues.body:
The code and Reasoning Gym tasks of `snowball-100k` are graded by scripts that run the reply's code in the same process that computes the reward, so a reply can score 1.0 without solving the task.

- `MarinSkyRL:eurus2_code` and `ultra_sft_step3200_comp_coding` use the vendored LiveCodeBench evaluator ([`livecodebench.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/scorers/livecodebench.py); the Ultra tasks ship the same file, [`graders.py` L99](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/graders.py#L99)). `grade_stdio` keeps the expected output in the local `gt_out` while the program runs ([L475](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/scorers/livecodebench.py#L475)), so a stdin program can find it on the stack and print it. Call-based tests compare with `prediction == gt_out` ([L417](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/scorers/livecodebench.py#L417)), so a return value whose `__eq__` always returns `True` passes. `reliability_guard` leaves both open; its docstring says it is not a security sandbox ([L676-L682](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/scorers/livecodebench.py#L676-L682)).
- Both Reasoning Gym grade scripts ([generated](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/reasoning_gym_grade.py#L58-L59), [Ultra](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/reasoning_gym_grade.py#L43)) print `score_reasoning_gym_answer(...)`, and grading reads the last line of stdout ([`grading.py` L356](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6fe54873e00d0669d0bb8a7ad818de0471cd94f/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L356)). The `n_queens` scorer of reasoning-gym 0.1.25 passes the reply to `eval` and `polynomial_multiplication` passes it to `sympy.parse_expr`, inside that process. A reply can register an `atexit` handler that prints `1.0`, write `1.0` and exit, or read the stored answer from `/tests/config.json`.

Impact: the two code sources are 22,722 of the 100,000 `snowball-100k` rows. Through each row's own grade script, on seeded samples, the frame-reading program below (the same text for every task) scored 1.0 on 53 of 53 stdin rows of `eurus2_code` and on 59 of 59 stdin rows of `comp_coding`, and the always-equal return scored 1.0 on 6 of 6 call-based `eurus2_code` rows. The `atexit` reply scored 1.0 on all 61 `n_queens` and `polynomial_multiplication` rows of the Ultra `reasoning_gym` component; the generated Reasoning Gym source has 1,000 entries of each of the two tasks.

Reproduce, from the repository root:

````bash
uv run --frozen --package marin-verifyit --with numpy==2.3.5 --with pandas==2.2.2 python - <<'EOF'
import json
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/scorers")
import livecodebench  # noqa: E402

STDIN = json.loads(
    livecodebench.normalize_lcb_ground_truth(
        [{"input": "1 2\n", "output": "3\n", "testtype": "stdin"}, {"input": "40 2\n", "output": "42\n", "testtype": "stdin"}]
    )
)
CALL = json.loads(
    livecodebench.normalize_lcb_ground_truth(
        [{"input": [1, 2], "output": 3, "testtype": "functional", "fn_name": "add"},
         {"input": [40, 2], "output": 42, "testtype": "functional", "fn_name": "add"}]
    )
)
FRAME_WALK = """import sys

frame = sys._getframe()
while frame is not None and "gt_out" not in frame.f_locals:
    frame = frame.f_back
print(frame.f_locals["gt_out"] if frame is not None else "", end="")"""
ALWAYS_EQUAL = """class _Any:
    def __eq__(self, other):
        return True

class Solution:
    def add(self, a, b):
        return _Any()"""


def fenced(code: str) -> str:
    return f"```python\n{code}\n```"


for label, tests, program in (
    ("stdin, correct a + b", STDIN, "a, b = map(int, input().split())\nprint(a + b)"),
    ("stdin, wrong (prints 0)", STDIN, "print(0)"),
    ("stdin, reads the expected output from the grader's frame", STDIN, FRAME_WALK),
    ("call-based, correct", CALL, "class Solution:\n    def add(self, a, b):\n        return a + b"),
    ("call-based, wrong (returns 0)", CALL, "class Solution:\n    def add(self, a, b):\n        return 0"),
    ("call-based, returns an object equal to everything", CALL, ALWAYS_EQUAL),
):
    _, reward = livecodebench.compute_score(fenced(program), tests)
    print(f"{reward}  {label}")
EOF
````

On main `c6fe54873` this prints:

```
1.0  stdin, correct a + b
0.0  stdin, wrong (prints 0)
1.0  stdin, reads the expected output from the grader's frame
1.0  call-based, correct
0.0  call-based, wrong (returns 0)
1.0  call-based, returns an object equal to everything
```

````bash
uv run --frozen --package marin-verifyit --extra reasoning-gym python - <<'EOF'
import json
import subprocess
import sys

import reasoning_gym

CHILD = """
import json, sys
from verifyit.modes.grade_reasoning_gym import score_reasoning_gym_answer
task, entry, reply = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
print(score_reasoning_gym_answer(task, entry, reply))
"""
REPLIES = {
    "n_queens": (
        "definitely wrong",
        "__import__('os').write(1, b'1.0\\n') and __import__('os')._exit(0)",
        "__import__('atexit').register(print, '1.0')",
    ),
    "polynomial_multiplication": ("definitely wrong", "__import__('atexit').register(print, '1.0')"),
}
for task, replies in REPLIES.items():
    entry = reasoning_gym.create_dataset(task, size=1, seed=7)[0]
    entry = {"question": entry["question"], "answer": entry["answer"], "metadata": entry["metadata"]}
    for reply in replies:
        child = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-c", CHILD], input=json.dumps([task, entry, reply]), capture_output=True, text=True
        )
        lines = child.stdout.split()
        print(f"{task}: exit {child.returncode}, stdout {lines}, last line read as reward: {lines[-1] if lines else None}  <- {reply!r}")
EOF
````

On main `c6fe54873` this prints:

```
n_queens: exit 0, stdout ['0.0'], last line read as reward: 0.0  <- 'definitely wrong'
n_queens: exit 0, stdout ['1.0'], last line read as reward: 1.0  <- "__import__('os').write(1, b'1.0\\n') and __import__('os')._exit(0)"
n_queens: exit 0, stdout ['0.0', '1.0'], last line read as reward: 1.0  <- "__import__('atexit').register(print, '1.0')"
polynomial_multiplication: exit 0, stdout ['0.0'], last line read as reward: 0.0  <- 'definitely wrong'
polynomial_multiplication: exit 0, stdout ['0.0', '1.0'], last line read as reward: 1.0  <- "__import__('atexit').register(print, '1.0')"
```

Expected: a reply scores what its output or answer earns. The program under test cannot read the expected output or return an object that decides the comparison, and a reply cannot write the reward line or read the stored answer.

cc @chrismc91 @penfever

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
#11985 (fixes #11984) moved RLVR-IFeval curation, the skyrl-gym `ifeval` path and Evalchemy harness IFEval onto verifyit's IFEval checks. It merged before two agent reviews arrived. Two defects from those reviews reproduce on `main` (bdeb84d638). Both change rewards and scores: harness IFEval protocol `2026.11.22` and `rlvr_ifeval` source version 2 now carry them.

**1. Harness `combination:repeat_prompt` fails compliant replies.** `_harness_constraint` (`lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/instructions.py:62-65`, called at `:40` and `:97`) puts the whole `spec.prompt` into `params["prompt"]`. The check at `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py:1077-1080` then requires a case-sensitive `text.startswith(prompt)`. The IFEval prompt includes the instruction sentence ("First repeat the request word for word … the request you need to repeat does not include this sentence"), and the source kwarg `prompt_to_repeat` holds only the request. The removed harness checker compared `value.strip().lower()` with `prompt_to_repeat.strip().lower()`; verifyit already uses those semantics in `lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/instruction_observations.py:205`. On `main`:

- a reply that repeats only the request, then answers: fail
- the same reply with the request in lowercase: fail
- a reply that echoes the full prompt, instruction sentence included, then answers: pass

So every IFEval prompt with this instruction scores 0 for a compliant model.

**2. Language constraints pass replies in the wrong language.** `validate_response_language` maps to `language:response_language` (`lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/adapters/open_instruct_ifeval.py:29`), and harness IFEval language prompts reach the same check. The check (`lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py:947-960`) passes on one closed-class hint word. On `main`, these English replies pass:

- "This is an English text about the band Die Antwoord." for `de`
- "Here is the a la carte menu in English." for `it`
- "This is a cafe de Paris mention." for `fr`

`experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/ifeval.py:63` already keeps this check out of `NEMOTRON_ARGUMENTS` for this reason, so `nemotron_if` rejects those rows. RLVR-IFeval and harness IFEval do not, so the RL reward pays for the wrong language and harness IFEval scores are inflated. #11985 removed `langdetect` from the harness image: `IFEVAL_GRADER = BASIC_GRADER` at `experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/environments.py:36`.

**3. A grading test no longer tests its claim.** The `("rlvr_ifeval", "nemotron_if_grade.py")` case of `test_grade_script_fails_rather_than_scoring_when_its_scorer_cannot_import` (`experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_skyrl_grading.py:64`) now replaces the grade script itself, not a scorer module that the script imports. It only checks that a crashing script is an infrastructure error, which the other cases already cover.

Done when:
- Harness `combination:repeat_prompt` grades against `prompt_to_repeat` with strip and case-insensitive comparison. A reply that repeats only the request, in any case, then answers, passes. A reply that answers without the repeat fails. A constraint without `prompt_to_repeat` fails closed.
- RLVR-IFeval rows with `validate_response_language` are rejected at conversion and at skyrl-gym preflight, as `nemotron_if` does. Harness IFEval grades `language:response_language` with a seeded language detector (for example `langdetect` in the harness grader image), not the hint-word check. The three English replies above fail for `de`, `it` and `fr`. A detector error fails closed.
- Regression tests cover each case above and fail on `bdeb84d638`.
- The stale `rlvr_ifeval` case at `test_skyrl_grading.py:64` is removed.
- The IFEval protocol version and the `rlvr_ifeval` source version are bumped, because scores change.

🤖

# Research

On `main` at `bdeb84d638`, harness conversion retains `prompt_to_repeat`, but `_harness_constraint` adds the full instruction prompt and verifyit's `combination:repeat_prompt` checks that full prompt as a case-sensitive prefix. The shared Open Instruct normalizer admits `validate_response_language` for both RLVR conversion and SkyRL preflight, while harness grading uses verifyit's hint-word check and its grader image lacks `langdetect`. No open PR matches #11986, `repeat_prompt`, or `response_language`.

**Relevant code**
- [`instructions.py#L62-L65`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bdeb84d638/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/instructions.py#L62-L65) — replaces the repeat target.
- [`ifeval.py#L947-L960`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bdeb84d638/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L947-L960) — accepts a language hint.
- [`ifeval.py#L1077-L1080`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bdeb84d638/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L1077-L1080) — checks the wrong repeat target.
- [`open_instruct_ifeval.py#L20-L29`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bdeb84d638/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/adapters/open_instruct_ifeval.py#L20-L29) — admits the language descriptor.
- [`data_contracts.py#L69-L78`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bdeb84d638/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/data_contracts.py#L69-L78) — shares normalization with preflight.

# Proposed Fix

1. Make `combination:repeat_prompt` read the source `prompt_to_repeat` without substituting the full prompt. Require a nonempty target; compare the stripped, lowercased reply prefix and require text after the repeat. Add harness tests for mixed case, missing repeat, and missing target.
2. Remove `validate_response_language` from the shared Open Instruct descriptor map, so RLVR conversion returns an unsupported-row rejection and SkyRL preflight raises on the same row. Add a conversion test and a `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-gym/tests/test_ifeval.py` preflight test.
3. Give harness IFEval its own `langdetect==1.0.9` grader dependency and a seeded (`DetectorFactory.seed = 0`) language check. Detector errors must score false. Test the `de`, `it`, and `fr` English counterexamples from the issue and an error case through harness grading; leave verifyit's stdlib-only generic check available to other callers.
4. Remove the stale `rlvr_ifeval` case from the scorer-import test. Bump the harness protocol from `2026.11.22` to `2026.11.22.1` and the `rlvr_ifeval` source version from `2` to `3`; run affected unit tests and repository lint before opening a PR with `Fixes #11986`.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Slow final hooks can turn completed optimizer updates and a saved final checkpoint into a failed multi-host job.

Reproduce:
1. Initialize two JAX processes with `shutdown_timeout_seconds=2`.
2. Delay process 0 for 5 seconds after computation, while process 1 calls `jax.distributed.shutdown()`.
3. Both processes abort. The shutdown barrier reports 1/2 processes present and process 0 missing. This CPU reproduction was run locally; it does not exercise GPU kernels or object-store uploads.

Observed on a 32-process H100 SFT run at source `cf9db0ac38e2f64eaa917979bbcc4efa98158b65` on 2026-11-22:
- Process 0 completed step 527 (528 updates) at 16:14:10UTC. Its native checkpoint committed at 16:15:27UTC; the HF export finished at 16:35UTC.
- Processes 1–31 logged completion of their final XLA-dump uploads at 16:39:33–43UTC. Process 0 has no corresponding upload-completion line.
- At16:41:33UTC, the shutdown barrier failed with 31/32 processes present. Process 27 entered first; process 0 was missing.
- Process 1's Python stack ends in `jax.distributed.shutdown()`, called by `_finalize_iris_jax_after_clean_exit`. Iris reports exit 139. The PyArrow/Torch names are the loaded-extension footer, not a causal stack.
- The task timeout was 72000 seconds. The failure occurred at the 120-second JAX shutdown deadline after the first process entered shutdown.
- The training completion receipt was not published. The exact operation delaying process 0 is not recoverable from the fatal signal-handler dump; final-hook/upload skew is supported by the logs, but an upload deadlock is not proven.

The relevant paths are [the Levanter exit handler](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cf9db0ac38e2f64eaa917979bbcc4efa98158b65/lib/levanter/src/levanter/distributed.py#L36), [the forced final hooks](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cf9db0ac38e2f64eaa917979bbcc4efa98158b65/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L738), [the synchronous dump uploader](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cf9db0ac38e2f64eaa917979bbcc4efa98158b65/lib/levanter/src/levanter/callbacks/profiler.py#L190), and [Iris's shutdown timeout](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cf9db0ac38e2f64eaa917979bbcc4efa98158b65/lib/iris/src/iris/jax/init.py#L48).

Expected: all processes finish required finalization before distributed shutdown starts. Publish the committed-checkpoint/control receipt before optional debug uploads. Bound those uploads and use a symmetric, bounded finalization rendezvous before shutdown. A delayed-process regression must preserve genuine training failures and must not relabel an unfinished checkpoint as complete.

Related closed incidents: #6907 and #7372 involved W&B teardown. This occurrence shows final-hook skew before the completion receipt; the process 0 blocker remains to be isolated.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`Trainer.train()` forces final hooks, and `run_hooks()` calls the XLA dump uploader synchronously on every rank after those hooks. Rank 0 calls Iris `complete_job` only after its JAX shutdown; 31/32 ranks entering the shutdown barrier establishes skew, but the blocked operation on rank 0 remains unknown. Iris `complete_job` marks unfinished tasks successful and stops them, so moving it before uploads would create a false success path.

**Relevant code**
- [`trainer.py#L372-L375`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/18a6cd6463ddb867378628d1ac4beba07cf33312/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L372-L375) — synchronous dump upload after hooks
- [`trainer.py#L420-L445`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/18a6cd6463ddb867378628d1ac4beba07cf33312/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L420-L445) — final checkpoint commit wait
- [`profiler.py#L190-L215`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/18a6cd6463ddb867378628d1ac4beba07cf33312/lib/levanter/src/levanter/callbacks/profiler.py#L190-L215) — unbounded per-file upload loop
- [`distributed.py#L36-L46`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/18a6cd6463ddb867378628d1ac4beba07cf33312/lib/levanter/src/levanter/distributed.py#L36-L46) — shutdown before job completion
- [`batches.py#L371-L399`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/18a6cd6463ddb867378628d1ac4beba07cf33312/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L371-L399) — completion stops unfinished tasks

# Proposed Fix

1. Log per-rank start and end of forced hooks, checkpoint wait, configured HF export, XLA upload, tracker finish, and JAX shutdown. Identify rank 0's delayed phase from a reproduction or retained logs before attributing this incident to an upload.
2. Split required finalization from optional diagnostics. Await the final native checkpoint commit and any required export before publishing a checkpoint-ready receipt with the completed step and checkpoint path. Keep Iris `complete_job` after coordinated shutdown.
3. Move the final XLA dump upload out of `run_hooks`; give the transfer a deadline that can stop blocked I/O, and record an upload timeout as a diagnostic failure. A thread wait alone cannot stop a blocked upload.
4. After each rank finishes required finalization and its bounded optional work, enter a named, bounded rendezvous before `jax.distributed.shutdown()`. A missing rank or failed required operation must fail the job and must not publish completion.
5. Add a real two-process CPU regression with rank 0 delayed beyond the JAX shutdown timeout, plus blocked-upload and failed-checkpoint cases. Verify successful runs publish one completion receipt, while required failures publish none; then validate the finalization sequence on a small H100 run with dump upload enabled.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 The [Nov 21 SkyRL nightly](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44925403052/job/136910257408) reached the Grug GPU suite: 33 tests passed, then `test_grug_megatron_eval_forward_is_independent_of_peer_rank_batch[toy_top4-pp1_ep2]` failed during Megatron optimizer initialization. The native traceback ends at `torch.distributed.all_gather_object` with NCCL `invalid usage`: “No algorithm/protocol nor symKernelId available for function AllGather ... NCCL_ALGO was set to allreduce:tree.” OPD and CatCount passed; this was a test/runtime failure after placement, not a cluster admission failure.

The repository's [batch-invariant worker settings](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb991a5a5c8af4d670d56757eeae3e59edd4a778/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/batch_invariant.py#L12-L23) set `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree`, and [Ray propagates that setting to the learner](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/cb991a5a5c8af4d670d56757eeae3e59edd4a778/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/utils/utils.py#L511-L514). [NCCL's syntax](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/env.html#nccl-algo) requires a default algorithm for functions outside a function-specific override. This setting leaves `AllGather` without one.

I’ll update the setting to permit Ring for other collectives while retaining Tree for all-reduce, then run the failing GPU case and the repository checks before opening a fix PR.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Triage complete. The [original failed Grug job](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44925403052/job/136910257408) reached the GPU suite and failed in `test_grug_megatron_eval_forward_is_independent_of_peer_rank_batch[toy_top4-pp1_ep2]`. Megatron's `all_gather_object` raised NCCL `invalid usage`: `NCCL_ALGO=allreduce:tree` gives AllGather no available algorithm. OPD and CatCount passed, and the Grug job was placed and running, so this is a batch-invariance configuration defect rather than an Iris infrastructure failure.

[PR #11956](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11956) supplies a Ring default for other collectives and preserves that setting after the pinned vLLM initializer overwrites it in SkyRL learner processes. The [targeted H100 rerun](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44930085809/job/136924588396) passed the exact failing case, with all three workflow lanes green. Affected local tests and PR CI passed.

The [full nightly rerun](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/44930544256/job/136927877372) passed the original case and the earlier four-GPU rollout case, then failed in `test_grug_megatron_four_gpu_disaggregated_rollout_train_sync_rollout[broadcast-32]`. Its vLLM inference engine core profiles the MoE model and calls `AllGather`; the native log again reports `NCCL_ALGO was set to allreduce:tree` and NCCL `invalid usage`. The separate engine process runs the [pinned vLLM initializer](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/0ac9dcb157ee/vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py#L1142-L1155), which hardcodes that setting. PR #11956 is therefore marked `Part of #11955`; it does not restore the full lane or close this issue.

To restore the lane, change the vLLM fork initializer to include a default algorithm (for example, `ring;allreduce:tree`), publish and qualify a new GPU wheel, adopt its exact pin in Marin, and rerun the full SkyRL nightly. This session's GitHub token has no access to `marin-community/vllm`, so the fork source/release step needs a maintainer with access. Issue #11955 remains open for that work.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Establish a versioned cold-start SFT recipe that runs immediately after pretraining cool-down. The recipe should produce a model with the core capabilities needed by Marin's post-training and evaluation workflows.

The initial competency set is:

- Chat-template adherence and basic instruction following.
- Think blocks.
- Thinking across science, mathematics, legal, and medical contexts.
- Adaptive thinking effort.
- Model-name responses.
- Basic agentic tool use.
- Answer-format hardening.
- Task summarization.
- Resuming a task from a summary.

Related preceding work: #7321 and #7743.

Research issues:

- #8093: adaptive thinking effort.
- #8094: model-name response behavior.
- #8092: answer-format hardening.
- #8095: task summarization.
- #8091: resume tasks from summaries.
- #8090: cross-domain thinking and basic agentic tool use.

Done when:

- A recipe version identifies its parent checkpoint, tokenizer and chat template, data mixture and immutable revisions, training configuration, and export contract.
- The recipe has acceptance evaluations for every listed competency, with recorded baseline comparisons and failure criteria.
- The recipe can be run after a pretraining cool-down without experiment-specific manual wiring.
- The selected recipe and its evidence are documented in the repository.

comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT tracking.** This issue now tracks cold-start SFT of the 535B-A23B Hero (Mochi) from its 262K checkpoint. Decision: use the 10.05 data. The SFT stage under Snowball v0.1 was 09.21, but 10.05 is the latest trained mix.

**Inputs**

- Start checkpoint: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491` ([#8435](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8435#issuecomment-6748198431)). `metadata.json` reads step 393491, not temporary. Size: 3.9 TB.
- Data: the 216-source "full A/B" mix of [Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05): 79.65% SFT and 20.35% replay, packed at 262,144 tokens.
  - Code: branch `held/grug-sft-full-ab-4750-grouped` at `ce7c77a`.
  - Manifest: `gs://marin-us-central2/grug_sft/stores/full-ab-packed-2026.09.29.json`.
  - The stores and tokenizer `2026.09.18` have CoreWeave copies in `s3://marin-us-east-02a`, the Hero's region.
- Tokenizer: the SFT tokenizer maps IDs 128005 and 128011 to `<tool_call>` and `</tool_call>`. The Hero pin `marin-tokenizer@a5ca45f` keeps them reserved. The run needs the 10.05 seven-row LM-head anchor initialization and must ship the 09.18 tokenizer.

**Blockers**

1. The checkpoint's model (log scaling, floor 65536, power 2) exists only on the branch of draft #11044, which carries #10986. Main's `HERO_MODEL` would load this checkpoint with the wrong attention scale on the global layers.
2. There is no full-model Hero SFT launcher. The Hero trainer already reads loss-weighted packed batches with segment IDs. The launcher must port four parts from the 10.05 trainer: the store mixture, the anchor rows, the √32 special-token LR and the frozen router bias.
3. Export and serving refuse log scaling ([#11056](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11056) B5). No PR adds it. Until one does, the SFT model cannot be served or evaluated through vLLM.
4. No SFT load test of a Hero 262K checkpoint has run (#11056 C3).

**Plan**

- Size: about 6,909 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions on 11 GB200 NVL72 racks (CP4 × EP16), which is one epoch of the SFT stores.
- Cost: about 57 h at the pretraining step time, and about 4.4e22 FLOPs.
- Checks before the full launch:
  - CPU tests of the port.
  - A 20-step one-rack load, save and restore test.
  - A step-0 offline eval at 262K, compared with the finalist's clean macro of 1.6434.
  - The #11056 memory gate: at most 180.75 of 184.30 GiB.

**Open decisions**

- Learning rate and gradient clip. 10.05 used 5e-5 with no warmup, decay over the last 10% and no clip.
- Replay source. Proposed: the Hero's 262K Harrier mix.
- Run ID and DRI.

🤖 Updates on the blockers in the comment above:

- **Blocker 1, resolved.** #11044 merged as 77f205bd2e, on top of #10986. Main's `HERO_MODEL` now has log scaling with floor 65536, slope 0.1 and power 2.0, so it loads the step-393491 checkpoint with the attention scale it was trained with. `CURRENT_HERO_RUN_ID` is `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`, and the launch commit is tagged `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`.
- **Blocker 3, still open, now being scoped.** #11056 is done and closing, so B5 moves to a new tracking issue, which I'll link here once filed. The scoping covers export and vLLM serving, and the SFT and RL model implementations, including per-document positions under sequence packing and context parallelism. Until it lands, the hero vibe check still works, because it samples from the native JAX model rather than vLLM.
- **Blocker 4, still open.** The model side no longer blocks it; it waits on the launcher (blocker 2).

For the step-0 check against 1.6434: that number is clean macro at 262K, the equal-weight mean over 19 Paloma and Uncheatable subsets (excluding ptb, wikitext_103, gab and twitterAAE), scored in 262,144-token windows. It comes from `launch_checkpoint_eval.py` on the `hero-mrcr-eval` branch. Since #10986, the floor, slope and power must be set together, so that script must pass `log_scaling_power=2.0` or it raises. More detail on the finalists: [logbooks #37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37#issuecomment-6751602983).

comments.author: ravwojdyla
comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT one-rack smoke tests, 2026-11-09.** The SFT procedure runs end to end on one GB200 rack, using the log-scaling model of #11044. It restores the Hero, reseeds the special tokens, trains on the 10.05 mix, saves and resumes. One recipe choice is open: with the router bias frozen as in 10.05, the Hero drops 5.8–8.1% of expert assignments.

**Setup**

- Shared by all runs:
  - start checkpoint `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491`;
  - 16 × 262,144 positions per update;
  - CP4 × EP16 on `cw-us-east-08a`;
  - MuonH 3.2905e-5 and Adam 7.5934e-6, the Hero's final 262K rates, with clip 1.0;
  - the 10.05 one-epoch block schedule with the Hero's 262K Harrier mix as replay.
- Code: local branch `rav/hero-sft-launcher` on the #11044 head `80cadd6858`, at `8dd7cef524`. It is not pushed yet.
  - It adds `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_hero_sft.py`.
  - It adds SFT options to the Hero trainer: router-bias mode, the special-token reseed with a √32 learning-rate scale, and `data_start_step`.
- Checkpoints are under `s3://marin-us-east-08a/tmp/ttl=3d/rav/` and expire after 3 days.

**Runs**

| Run | Router bias | W&B | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v1 | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v1) | Failed before the first update. Restore and reseed worked. Building the eval sets then asked each SFT store for a `validation` split, and the stores hold only `train`. Fixed by reading each store as a flat cache of its `train/` directory. |
| A, 20 updates | frozen | [hero-sft-smoke-v2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v2) | Passed. Saved step-393511 (3.9 TB); details below. |
| B, resume A to 25 updates | frozen | same run as A | Passed. All 64 ranks loaded the run's own step-393511, did not reseed again, resumed the same W&B run, and saved step-393516. |
| C, 20 updates | update | [hero-sft-smoke-v3-update](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v3-update) | Passed. |

Smoke A details:

- Restore took about 2 min.
- All ranks reseeded the 7 special-token LM-head columns, with anchors {128006: 3560, 128007: 1984, 128002: 1781, 128003: 4320, 128005: 5507, 128011: 842, 128009: 128001}.
- Caches for the 415 components built in 1m13s.

**Measurements**

| | A: frozen | C: update | Finalist at the end of pretraining |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drop fraction | 5.8% (step 393500) to 8.1% (393509) | 1e-4 to 3e-5 | about 2e-4 |
| Train loss at step 393500 (the same batch in both arms) | 0.646 | 0.698 | 0.81–0.95 |
| Gradient norm at step 393500 | 1.56 (clipped) | 1.65 (clipped) | about 0.17 |
| Dropless eval loss on Paloma after 20 updates | 1.712; macro 2.0399 | 1.742 | macro 2.0358 |
| Step time and peak memory | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 23 s, 130.77 GiB | 29 s at 11 racks, 130.77 GiB |

**Findings**

- Snowball's SFT also froze the router bias. It ran with expert axis 1, and `capacity_overflow_rate_mean` is 0 in every Snowball SFT run. The Hero runs EP16 at capacity factor 1.5, so a frozen bias drops tokens.
- With the bias updating, the drops disappear. Train loss on the same batch and Paloma eval loss are higher over the first 20 updates. Twenty updates do not show which mode gives the better SFT model.
- The trainer's first-step eval never fires on a restored run. With `--eval-every 500`, the first SFT eval comes at step 393500.

**Open before the 11-rack launch**

- Router-bias mode. The launcher now requires `--router-bias`.
- Learning rate and clip, run identity and DRI.
- Merge #10986 and #11044, then land the launcher.
- Serving support for log scaling (#11056 B5), before the SFT model can be evaluated through vLLM.

At 11 racks the plan is 6,916 updates of 176 × 262,144 positions, about 57 h.

comments.body:
🤖 **Hero SFT plan, 2026-11-10.** The launcher and the expert placement are on `main` (#11136, #11149). The proposed run below does one epoch of the 10.05 mix on 11 racks. On one rack, this configuration drops 0.56% of expert assignments with a frozen router bias. Without the placement, the drop rate is 3.60%. Gate 1 needs sign-off and gates 3 and 4 need a reviewer.

**Proposed parameters (gate 1)**

| Parameter | Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start checkpoint | `hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491` | Latest checkpoint from #8435; `metadata.json` step 393491 |
| Data | 10.05 full A/B mix: 216 CoreWeave stores, one epoch each | Latest validated mix; used as it is, without the Open-SWE fixes |
| Replay | Hero 262K Harrier mix, `--replay-fraction 0.2035` (20.43% at 11 racks) | 10.05 replay is Snowball pretraining data |
| Router bias | `frozen` (launcher default) | 10.05 recipe |
| Capacity factor | 1.625 | Highest that fits in memory; see below |
| Expert placement | `hero_sft_expert_placement_step393491.json` | Cuts drops from 3.60% to 0.56% |
| MuonH rate | 3.2905e-5 | Hero's final pretraining rate (1% of peak) |
| Adam rate | 3.2905e-5 | 10.05's pattern: one rate for both groups. Lower train loss, same eval |
| Gradient clip | 1.0 | Hero's clip; 10.05 used none |
| Topology | 11 racks, CP4 × EP16, 176 × 262,144 positions per update | |

The Adam rate applies to all `token_embed` rows, the router weights, `attn_gate` and the norm gains. The √32 update scale for the seven special tokens is separate.

**One-rack evidence.** All runs start from step-393491 on the same data order, frozen, MuonH 3.2905e-5, clip 1.0, 100 updates.

| Arm | Placement | cf | Adam | Train loss | Drops | Final dropless eval / Paloma macro |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf1625) (proposed) | yes | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5510 | 0.56% | 1.7089 / 2.0336 |
| [A](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-placed-cf15) | yes | 1.5 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5524 | 0.89% | 1.7090 / 2.0338 |
| [B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625) | no | 1.625 | 3.29e-5 | 0.5581 | 3.60% | 1.7090 / 2.0336 |
| [4](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-100-noplace-cf1625-adam7e6) | no | 1.625 | 7.59e-6 | 0.5613 | 3.67% | 1.7090 / 2.0343 |

- The order 1 < A < B < 4 holds in every 25-update quarter. The placement came from updates 1–25 of an earlier smoke, and A's drops stay flat through update 100.
- All arms run at 23.5–23.8 s/step with a peak of 130.8 GiB, the same as pretraining.
- Dropless eval loss does not separate the arms. Paloma macro improves from about 2.0386 at the first eval (step 393499) to about 2.034 in all four; the finalist ended at 2.0358.
- Arm A resumed from its own placed checkpoint, and no rank placed the experts or reseeded the special tokens a second time.
- Capacity factor: 1.75 and 2.0 fail the rematerialization check during compile. 1.6875, and 1.75–2.0 with a higher slop factor, compile but run out of memory in the first NCCL all-to-all. A higher factor needs a memory-layout change.

**Plan on `main` (`7521ea658f`).** Dry run: 6,916 updates (steps 393491–400407), 19 mixture blocks of 64,064 sequences, linear decay to 0.1× over the last 692 updates. That is 319.1B positions and about 4.4e22 FLOPs. At pretraining's 29.9 s/step on 11 racks, the run takes about 57 h. Checkpoints go under `expert-placement-1e80fa529585/` at 3.9 TB each, with one temporary resume checkpoint plus the final one.

```bash
IRIS_USER=marin uv run iris --config lib/iris/config/marin.yaml job run --no-wait --enable-extra-resources \
  --target-cluster cw-us-east-08a --priority system --system-reason "hero SFT" \
  --cpu 1 --memory 4g --max-retries 1000 --job-name hero-sft-fullab-step393k-coord \
  -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" -e IRIS_PORT_JAX 32614 \
  -- python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch_hero_sft \
    --run-id hero-sft-fullab-step393k \
    --initialize-from-checkpoint s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-393491 \
    --muon-lr 3.2905e-5 --adam-lr 3.2905e-5 --max-grad-norm 1.0 --replay-fraction 0.2035 \
    --dp-racks 11 --capacity-factor 1.625 \
    --expert-placement experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_sft_expert_placement_step393491.json \
    --eval-every 500 --version 2026.11.10 --run
```

**Gates**

1. ⏸️ Select params: proposed above, needs sign-off.
2. ✅ SFT launcher on `main`: #11136 and #11149 merged, and the dry run above passes on `main`.
3. ⏸️ SFT data reviewed: needs a reviewer to accept the known caveats:
   - re-closed reasoning spans (#10400);
   - reward hacking in 17.3% of successful Open-SWE traces (#10865);
   - looping reasoning in 15.6% of sampled tokens ([report card](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1569187938154057781)).
4. ⏸️ SFT smoke run reviewed: the arms above ran #11149 at `2f30fb76e9`. The merged #11149 also records the placement in each checkpoint's metadata and refuses a restore whose placement does not match. One short smoke and resume from `main` will confirm that path before kick-off.

Also before kick-off:

- 11 GB200 racks agreed with the Hero owners, and a `system`-priority submitter confirmed.
- Run ID (proposed `hero-sft-fullab-step393k`), DRI and babysitter named.
- vLLM evals of the SFT model need the log-scaling export (#11127).

**First-hour abort criteria** (from arm 1)

| Signal | Expected | Stop the run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Restore | All ranks load step-393491 and log one placement and one reseed | A rank missing, or a second placement or reseed after a restart |
| Train loss | 0.4–0.7 | NaN, or at least 1.25 |
| Gradient norm | Below 1 on most steps; single spikes to about 8 | Above 10, or above 5 for several steps |
| Drop fraction | About 0.6%, under 2% per step | Above 3% sustained, or rising |
| Step time | About 29 s | Above 35 s sustained |
| First eval | Paloma macro within 0.01 of 2.0358 | Above 2.06 |
