Means: native equal-20 23.17% against 19.12% (+4.05 pp; spreads 2.98 and 3.06 pp); mass 99.12 against 87.29 (+11.83). Harbor trials scored of 100: 10% 99 and 99; 20.47% 99 and 100.

🤖

## Mochi launcher results: baseline, 20% replay and 5% replay on 13 evaluations

Three Mochi models, scored with the evaluation launcher from PR 11528 (head `b3611d8a`): the sealed step-400407 baseline, and the 20% and 5% replay models (8-hour arms, step 401600). Each model ran on its own vLLM server (16 GB200 GPUs, data parallel 16). These are launcher rows. Compare Mochi only with Mochi on this launcher.

## Row rules
- `--limit 100`: the first 100 source items of each evaluation (AIME24: 30 problems x 10 trials = 300 samples; GPQA-Diamond: 100 questions x 3 trials = 300). One trial per item elsewhere.
- Reply cap 16,384 tokens, 32 concurrent requests per evaluator, one evaluator at a time. Thinking on for AIME24, GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro and MATH-500; off for the other nine.
- **A reply cut at its cap counts as wrong**, whatever letter or answer the grader extracted. The cap is 16,384 tokens, except CRUXEval (2,048) and NUPA5K-loose (256), whose tasks set their own. Unscored items would also count as wrong; none are unscored here.
- The launcher's own score is shown beside the capped score where they differ. It credits answers extracted from cut-off replies.
- Flags: 10% or more of replies cut at the cap means "cap-bound" and the row is not used to rank. If two models' cut shares differ by 5 points or more, the row is "cap-affected".

## Results (capped score; launcher score in brackets where different)

| Evaluation (items) | Baseline | 20% | 5% | Cut at cap (baseline / 20% / 5%) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIME24 (300) | 63.00% (64.33%) | 63.67% (64.67%) | 62.00% (63.33%) | 108 / 105 / 110 | cap-bound, unranked |
| GPQA-Diamond (300) | 57.67% (72.00%) | 61.67% (73.67%) | 58.67% (70.33%) | 108 / 104 / 108 | cap-bound, unranked |
| MMLU-Pro (100) | 61.00% | 67.00% | 63.00% (65.00%) | 3 / 2 / 4 | usable |
| MATH-500 (100) | 94.00% | 96.00% | 96.00% | 4 / 3 / 1 | usable |
| GSM8K 0-shot, flexible-extract (100) | 77.00% | 79.00% | 82.00% | 0 / 0 / 0 | usable (strict-match is 0.00% for all three: its pattern never matches these replies) |
| TriviaQA, extract_answer (100) | 73.00% | 65.00% | 66.00% | 0 / 0 / 0 | usable |
| TruthfulQA, acc (100) | 70.20% | 70.62% | 70.35% | 0 / 0 / 0 | usable |
| HumanEval+ (100) | 85.00% | 89.00% | 90.00% | 0 / 0 / 0 | usable |
| MBPP+ (100) | 82.00% | 77.00% | 78.00% | 0 / 0 / 0 | usable |
| CRUXEval (100) | 90.00% | 87.00% | 84.00% (85.00%) | 2 / 4 / 3 | usable |
| IFBench, strict prompt (100) | 37.00% | 36.00% | 35.00% | 0 / 0 / 0 | usable |
| MRCR, accuracy (100) | 28.27% | 30.40% | 23.46% | 0 / 0 / 0 | usable |
| NUPA5K-loose, exact match (100) | 15.00% | 12.00% | 16.00% | 48 / 51 / 54 | cap-bound at its 256-token task cap, cap-affected, unranked |

Among the replies that were not cut, AIME24 is correct on 98.44% / 97.95% / 97.89% (baseline / 20% / 5%) and GPQA-Diamond on 90.10% / 94.39% / 91.67%. On GPQA-Diamond the launcher's own score credits 43 / 36 / 35 cut replies, which is why it is far above the capped score.

## Notes
- **Code evaluations.** In the first full runs, HumanEval+, MBPP+ and CRUXEval could not be graded on this branch: the grader's setup step ran before the answer file was installed (fixed on `main` by `1a8a628d26`, PR 11408). The three code rows come from reruns with that commit cherry-picked onto the PR head; the replies are fresh samples, not re-grades. All other rows come from the first runs on the PR head alone.
- **Replaced baseline run.** The first baseline rerun of the code evaluations was replaced: its server failed to start, so it was cancelled and launched again.
- **Transient errors.** A few single requests hit a connection error at the model call (MMLU-Pro once per model; also single items in GSM8K, TriviaQA and NUPA5K-loose in some runs). Each recovered on its first retry, and every item is scored in every row.

## What this does not show
- Each usable row is 100 items, one trial per item, one run per model, with no seed replicate (AIME24 and GPQA-Diamond run 10 and 3 trials per item, and are unranked). Differences of a few points are inside what one run of this size can resolve.
- AIME24, GPQA-Diamond and NUPA5K-loose are unranked, because 35 to 54% of replies hit their cap.
- It does not show why any model differs from another: nothing here separates training changes from sampling noise.

## Reading
On the usable rows the 20% and 5% models are mostly within a few points of each other (the largest gaps are MRCR, 30.40% vs 23.46%, and MMLU-Pro, 67% vs 63%), within what a single n=100 run resolves. Against the baseline, both 8-hour models score lower on TriviaQA (65% and 66% vs 73%), MBPP+ (77% and 78% vs 82%) and CRUXEval (87% and 84% vs 90%), and higher on HumanEval+ (89% and 90% vs 85%).

## Result

- **Held-out loss:** r0's SFT loss is higher than both (0.5912 vs 0.5032 for P1 and 0.5016 for arm E r2). The identity-data set is much higher (2.3100 vs 1.2696 and 1.1933), while the Nemotron SFT v3 macro and agenttrove losses are slightly lower. On the pooled SFT loss, r0 is about equal (0.2228 vs 0.2255 and 0.2229). Its pretrain macro loss is slightly higher (0.8618 vs 0.8597 and 0.8578).
- **Edit-call:** The r0 and P1 intervals overlap for every reported rate (pooled applied edits 0.806 vs 0.774). r0 is higher than arm E r2 on every tool-call, parse, strict-format and applied-edit rate, with non-overlapping intervals (pooled applied edits 0.806 vs 0.642).

**Across the three measures:** Compared with P1, r0 had higher held-out SFT loss, with the largest increase on identity-data. All reported edit-call intervals overlapped, and r0 averaged 2.37 percentage points lower on equal-weight Micro210. Across the three replay shares, the Micro210 means are not monotonic (52.32%, 54.69%, 51.75%), so we claim no replay trend. ### Replies with no edit call (description only)

A reply counts here when the scorer found no edit call in it, either parsed by the server or written in the text.

| run | greedy (of 171) | sampled, pooled (of 855) | JSON inside `<tool_call>` parses once one closing brace is added | once two closing braces are added | single-quoted string after a key | other JSON error | no `<tool_call>` tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r0 | 19 | 87 | 11 | 1 | 21 | 53 | 20 |
| P1 | 16 | 98 | 8 | 0 | 21 | 82 | 3 |
| arm E r2 | 46 | 233 | 9 | 0 | 17 | 100 | 153 |

- The shape columns count greedy and sampled replies together.

## Micro210

Two inference repeats of one checkpoint each, all scored on cw-rno2a.

| 14 clean sources | equal-weight mean, repeat 1 / repeat 2 (mean, spread) | mass of 340, repeat 1 / repeat 2 (mean, spread) |
|---|---|---|
| r0 (0%) | 52.47% / 52.16% (52.32%, 0.31 pp) | 138.12 / 135.93 (137.03, 2.20) |
| P1 (10%) | 55.57% / 53.81% (54.69%, 1.76 pp) | 147.19 / 138.20 (142.70, 9.00) |
| arm E r2 (20.47%) | 51.99% / 51.51% (51.75%, 0.49 pp) | 144.22 / 136.11 (140.16, 8.11) |
| r0 − P1 | −2.37 pp | −5.67 |
| r0 − arm E r2 | +0.57 pp | −3.14 |

- **Against P1:** both P1 repeats are above both r0 repeats on the equal-weight mean (53.81 to 55.57% against 52.16 to 52.47%). On mass, the highest r0 repeat is 0.08 below the lowest P1 repeat, and the gap (−5.67) is smaller than the P1 mass spread (9.00).
- **Against arm E r2:** both r0 repeats are above both arm E r2 repeats on the equal-weight mean by a small margin (the lowest r0 repeat is 0.17 pp above the highest arm E r2 repeat). The mass ranges overlap.
- These describe two repeats per model; they are not a statistical separation or a resolved replay effect.
- **All 20 sources:** r0 41.30%, P1 41.46%, arm E r2 40.14%; the three means span 1.31 pp. The excluded Harbor trials differ (r0 4 and 2; P1 1 and 1; arm E r2 5 and 3).
- **Length:** r0 averages 9,081 and 8,825 response tokens per sequence (P1 9,138 and 9,040; arm E r2 8,970 and 9,006).

## Limits

- One training run per model. The edit-call intervals cover file-level sampling only, and the two Micro210 repeats cover inference only; neither measures training-seed variation. The held-out losses have no interval.
- r0 vs P1 changes only the replay share (and bookkeeping). Comparisons with arm E r2 also change the training code; the two cannot be separated.
- No causal claim. The evidence does not show why the 10% run scores above the other two on Micro210.
- One-hour rows only.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
The SkyRL CPU launcher can select a cached Python build without Linux pidfd support and fail before evaluation workers start.

Reproduce:
1. Run a Linux task whose image provides a compatible Python with `os.pidfd_open`, while the shared uv cache contains a compatible managed build without that API.
2. Use `skyrl_cpu_command` to construct a rollout worker in the frozen SkyRL CPU environment.
3. Observe that uv selects the managed build and Shellbox keeper allocation raises `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'pidfd_open'`.

Expected: nested SkyRL interpreter selection follows the task image's compatible system interpreter, and worker preflight verifies the required pidfd capability before allocating GPUs.

In the observed case, task setup selected image CPython 3.12.16, but the nested environment selected cached CPython 3.12.12. Both processes ran on Linux. `--no-python-downloads` prevents a download; it does not prevent selection of an existing managed build. Iris task setup already prefers the image interpreter, but the nested SkyRL launcher does not.

The branch fix is [1e1d04c3c2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/1e1d04c3c2ebb9791ee2a224a5e839b34ae583d3). A real-uv regression fails against the unchanged launcher and passes with the fix. A Linux CPU qualification built the real rollout worker with the original evaluation document on image CPython 3.12.16.

spillover_issues.author: Helw150
spillover_issues.body:
**Looking for the data?**

- [David’s cluster 22 handoff](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-cluster22-reconstruction/docs/reproducibility/hero-cluster22-handoff.md#inspect-the-result) lists the private reconstructed text and access instructions: **150 sources and 151,474,843 selected document occurrences**, preserving repeated selections.
- [The checked-in data references](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/datakit/hero_data.py) identify existing pipeline artifacts.
- **There is no public Hugging Face metadata release yet.** The [release proposal](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-cluster22-reconstruction/docs/reproducibility/hero-metadata-release-proposal.md) describes the planned tables.

Marin’s data is reproducible in principle, but reproducing it still requires expensive scans and pipeline runs. We want a cheap path that reuses existing selection decisions, scores and embeddings.

David’s handoff completed text reconstruction for cluster 22. Our follow-up work checked output counts and stored Harrier coverage, and is adding foreign keys to original source rows or records, alongside document IDs, cluster and quality metadata, and stored vectors.

Validated metadata now covers **31 of 150 sources in cluster 22, totaling 9,530,758 selected occurrences**. This includes all selected Nemotron Code v2 **synthetic Code Review (4,932,132)**, **synthetic Rewriting (3,447,382)** and **synthetic Student-Teacher (1,150,817)** documents, with keys to their original sources and physical rows, selection metadata and stored Harrier vectors. Full output audits checked every exported file and source coordinate for all three sources.

QA’s original-row mappings are complete. Its final source index and vector join remain unfinished. The full cluster 22 metadata export remains in progress. Where identical text matches several upstream rows, we retain alternatives without claiming to know which historical occurrence supplied the document.

We plan to publish metadata, stored embeddings, manifests and reconstruction instructions on Hugging Face. Users should be able to retrieve upstream inputs and reconstruct the selected corpus without repeating deduplication, contamination checks, classifiers, embedding inference or clustering. Cluster 22 is the first validation target; the goal covers all 40 topic clusters.

We do not plan to republish upstream text or tokens. Retrieval stays upstream to preserve attribution and creators’ control over removals and opt-outs. Pinned revisions cannot guarantee access to removed data.

Done when the metadata is accessible, source/vector joins and selected counts are validated, and a worked reconstruction example reports time, bytes read and compute.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
Micro210 TruthfulQA rows list a correct answer as option A in every row, so a model that always answers "A" scores 1.0. The frozen prepared rows keep TruthfulQA's source order, which puts the true answers first. The Exp5 SFT step-527 Micro210 run scored 1.00 on `truthfulqa_truthful_qa`; earlier runs scored 0.90 and 0.70. These scores measure how often the model picks A.

Reproduce:
1. Read `rollouts.parquet` from `open-athena/micro210-prepared-tasks@d8fa0e259ae63b1978388b20a17f72036642dd05`.
2. Select the 10 rows whose benchmark is TruthfulQA.
3. Read the options in each prompt. Option A is a true answer in all 10, for example "A. It doesn't tell us anything about global warming." and "A. The word \"chav\" is not an acronym."

Expected: options are shuffled with a fixed, recorded seed per row, and the grader accepts only the shuffled letters of the true answers.

Done when:
- TruthfulQA option order in the Micro210 build is a seeded permutation, recorded per row, and the grader scores against the permuted letters.
- The other multiple-choice rows in Micro210 (GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro and any other lettered-choice benchmark) are checked for the same fixed-position bias, and fixed the same way where present.
- A regression test fails when the correct option sits at one fixed position for every row of a benchmark.
- The fix ships as a new Micro210 policy version. The frozen version is not edited in place, and the change note lists which benchmark scores change.

GPQA-Diamond keys are A:1/B:5/C:2/D:2 and MMLU-Pro keys are A:1/B:2/E:1/G:1/I:4/J:1 across their 10 tasks; neither has one universally correct position. Publish a new immutable policy and prepared-table revision with the changed score scope. The existing policy and prepared commits remain pinned for historical runs.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The prepared Micro210 table preserves TruthfulQA's source choice order, so all 10 selected tasks accept A; the [prior constant-reply audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11337#issuecomment-7041057634) measured 100% for constant A, 50% for constant B on GPQA-Diamond, and 40% for `I don't know.` on MMLU-Pro. GPQA already shuffles source answers deterministically, but the selected keys are concentrated at B; MMLU-Pro preserves source labels. The [current Micro210 policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e1742c045d2ce976c6c8a78d1cf9beb439f054c3/experiments/evaluation/micro210_policy.py#L13-L53) and [launcher input check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e1742c045d2ce976c6c8a78d1cf9beb439f054c3/experiments/evaluation/micro210.py#L73-L78) pin the prepared bytes, so correcting rows requires a new policy and prepared-task revision.

**Relevant code**
- [`build_release_dataset.py#L340-L416`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b53a4d12e9f55bb2c629c7423a00974ec1df4d7/experiments/evaluation/mini_policy/build_release_dataset.py#L340-L416) — archived Micro210/Mini840 release builder.
- [`reasoning.py#L161-L222`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e1742c045d2ce976c6c8a78d1cf9beb439f054c3/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/reasoning.py#L161-L222) — GPQA permutation and MMLU-Pro labels.
- [`micro210_inputs.py#L87-L96`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e1742c045d2ce976c6c8a78d1cf9beb439f054c3/experiments/evaluation/micro210_inputs.py#L87-L96) — prepared table rebinding.

# Design

1. Audit the pinned 210 source tasks and 440 prepared rollouts with their actual graders. Enumerate every lettered-choice benchmark, count accepted letters per benchmark, and run each constant-letter reply. Record the source revision and counts; distinguish an all-one-position defect from the smaller-cohort imbalance tracked in [#11829](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11829).
2. Add a versioned preparation transform for TruthfulQA. Derive a per-task seed from the policy version and stable source task ID, record it in the row manifest, and apply one permutation to displayed choices and the verifier's choice/true-label pairs. Preserve every true answer when a task has multiple accepted choices. Apply the same transform to any other benchmark the audit finds fixed at one position; keep the full-policy likelihood scorer unchanged, as scoped in [#11827](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11827).
3. Add a release gate that fails when any letter is accepted by every task in a lettered-choice benchmark. Test repeatability, prompt/verifier agreement through the real grader, and preservation of multi-answer TruthfulQA labels. Report each benchmark's before/after letter counts and best constant-reply score; handle the non-uniform GPQA and MMLU-Pro cohorts with #11829's selection work where no fixed-position defect exists.
4. Build new immutable prepared-task and Micro210 policy revisions. Pin the new Hugging Face commit, byte size, and SHA-256 in the launcher; retain historical references and records. Publish a change note naming each benchmark whose scores can change, the old/new constant-reply floors, and a paired re-score of existing model outputs when available.
